_comment: agent_harness governance. Written BEFORE the harness, then signed; the harness is built to fit it. Every key is read by the engine (tools/check_govern_keys.py) and every section says what it is FOR here. Sections of govern-template.json left out are listed with the reason in README.md ('Considered and omitted').
description: Governed multi-agent audit harness: planner -> worker (tools) -> verify -> critics -> judge -> report
_comment_security: standard: no absolute paths, no fork/exec for NAAb code. Not restricted -- restricted removes FS_READ outright and filesystem.mode cannot give it back; the harness must read its fixtures.
_comment_governance: Config equivalents of CLI flags. Reports land in the run directory. Overrides must carry a reason (and the override flag itself is locked below).
_comment_runtime: Whole-run wall clock. A live run of ~10 model calls needs well under this; a hung provider does not get to hold the run open.
_comment_integrity: Locked CLI flags. --tree-walk is locked because taint through a function ARGUMENT is enforced on the VM and missed by the tree-walker; the rest would loosen governance from the command line. A signed config also blocks --no-governance/--governance-override implicitly. The locks hold for everyone, the key holder included (measured on this build); to change what is allowed, edit this file and re-sign it.
_comment_trust: Authority decay. A signature older than 30 days is a HARD stop: re-review and re-sign rather than run on a stale lock.
_comment_contradiction_detection: A locked config that contradicts itself must not run: max_level hard. (CONTRA-013 is hardcoded advisory and fires whenever sandbox_level is not restricted -- noise here, languages are all blocked.)
_comment_prerequisites: The provider key must exist before the first model call, not fail on it.
_comment_languages: Two polyglot steps, nothing else. python: an AST cross-check of the workspace (a second, mechanical ground truth beside truth.json). javascript: renders the summary table. Everything else is blocked, PHP included -- it reads blocked paths even at sandbox standard (measured). Both allowed runtimes are in-process: an embedded <<python>> open() is checked against capabilities.filesystem by the audit hook (the same decision file.read() gets), and QuickJS has no filesystem API. per_language: only keys an engine check reads are set -- timeout, max_lines, banned_functions, imports.blocked, no_var. imports.mode 'allowlist' / imports.allowed are parsed but NOT enforced (only the blocked list is checked), so the blocklist is explicit. per_language imports.blocked is ALSO installed as a runtime __import__ hook, which sees the standard library's own imports -- ast and json import os, sys, builtins and importlib internally (measured), so those four are blocked statically in restrictions.imports instead -- and so is io, which the executor's OWN stdout capture imports (blocking it at runtime breaks every later block: measured, 'Failed to get __main__ module').
_comment_polyglot: Every NAAb value a block uses must be bound explicitly (<<python[name]), so what crosses into a block is visible in the source and reaches taint tracking. The other polyglot.* keys in the template (max_bound_variables, require_json_pipe, max_output_lines, context_isolation, ...) have no engine consumer and are omitted.
_comment_codegen: No runtime code execution: model output is data, never code.
_comment_capabilities: network: off for NAAb code (http.* is a HARD block); agent provider calls are made by the engine and are governed per agent (network_allowed), not by this switch -- measured. shell: off at the SANDBOX layer, the only containment that survives a renamed binary. filesystem: the three harness directories; govern.json/.sig/trusted keys are added to blocked_paths automatically. env_vars: NAAB code may not read or write the environment at all -- the engine reads the provider key itself. functions: least privilege per function, INTERSECTED down the call stack; default grants nothing; main {} runs under default.
_comment_limits: Bounds on the NAAb program itself. Only enforced limits are set (limits.data.string_length/dict_size/nesting_depth and execution.total_executions are parsed but read by nothing).
_comment_requirements: The program must have a main block. (naming_conventions is omitted: no check reads it for NAAb source -- measured, a camelCase variable passes.)
_comment_restrictions: Pattern restrictions on the polyglot source (dangerous calls, injection, obfuscation, exfiltration shapes, resource abuse, privilege escalation, weak crypto) plus the two families that also run on NAAb's own calls. Static, so evadable by construction -- the runtime half is the audit hook and the in-process runtimes' lack of other capabilities. NOTE: dangerous_calls, privilege_escalation, code_injection and crypto are enabled by PRESENCE; 'enabled: false' would not turn them off.
_comment_taint: Model output is untrusted. It reaches a file -- or a polyglot block (python_exec/javascript_exec sinks) -- only through a sanitize_ function. Agent output is tainted whenever taint is on, whatever 'sources' lists; a dict holding ANY tainted value is tainted as a whole. lineage records where each taint came from (shows in the violation).
_comment_code_quality: Only the checks that run on NAAb code are set. Agent RESPONSES: no_secrets and no_pii (both OFF unless enabled; HARD ends the run). Harness FUNCTION BODIES: placeholders (comments included), oversimplification, incomplete logic (with the cosmetic-sanitizer check on sanitize_ functions), a complexity floor on the verifier, duplicate calls, and declared intent per function. The other code_quality checks (dead code, mock data, encoding, path traversal, hardcoded urls/ips/results, debug artifacts, ...) scan polyglot blocks only -- measured, inert here.

rules.message: The verifier must contain real logic -- a hollowed-out verifier passes every claim

code_quality._comment_polyglot_checks: These scan the polyglot blocks (the Python analyzer and the JavaScript renderer); they do not read NAAb source. semantic_checks adds the object-graph escape patterns (__subclasses__ and friends) on top of banned_functions.

intent_validation.project_intent: Audit code in a workspace with governed agents and verify every claim against ground truth

function_intents.list_files: list_dir the workspace files and count them
function_intents.read_file: read a workspace file path and number its lines
function_intents.load_json: read and parse a json file path
function_intents.plan_problems: check the plan steps count and that each step has an id and a goal; return the problems
function_intents.load_sources: read each python file named in truth files from the workspace into sources
function_intents.analyze_sources: parse sources with python ast and find division by len, range from one, and open outside with
function_intents.check_fixture: check every truth defect is among the static findings within line tolerance; return agree and missing
function_intents.sanitize_stats: sanitize step results into integer counts per step and totals
function_intents.render_summary: render the stats as a markdown table with javascript
function_intents.make_plan: propose plan candidates, select_admissible steps, commit the selected plan
function_intents.verify_claims: verify claimed files and defects against truth within line tolerance; return passed, verified, rejected
function_intents.run_step: send the step goal to the worker, parse claims, verify_claims against truth, record_validation
function_intents.review: fan_out the summary to critics, parse each verdict, consensus_vote the votes
function_intents.adjudicate: send the summary and tally to the judge and parse the verdict
function_intents.sanitize_report: sanitize report text by bounding its length
function_intents.write_report: stringify the report, sanitize_report it, write the report and the summary files

_comment_contracts: Structural and behavioural guarantees on the harness functions, checked by the engine, not by review. must_call: ground truth reaches governance, nothing reaches a file unsanitized, plans are selected and committed. must_produce: golden tests on the PURE verifier -- a verifier that passes everything (or nothing) fails the run. Arity pins tool signatures to their schemas.

run_step.description: Every worker step reports its ground-truth result to governance

write_report.description: Reports are sanitized before they are written

analyze_sources.description: The Python analyzer finds each defect shape, and nothing in clean code

check_fixture.description: Ground truth must agree with the static analysis, or the fixture is wrong

sanitize_stats.description: Only integer counts leave the sanitizer

render_summary.description: The JavaScript renderer returns the summary text

make_plan.description: Plans are selected from candidates and committed, never taken raw

verify_claims.description: Pure verifier: accepts what ground truth holds, rejects what it does not

rejected: defect not in ground truth: a.py:9

plan_problems.description: Pure plan shape check: 1-4 steps, each with an id and a goal

expect: step 1 lacks an id or a goal

_comment_agents: Each system_prompt opens with a unique AH-<ROLE> token (the local stub routes on it). allowed_actions is the per-role action matrix; tools are dual-gated (listed here AND registered in harness.naab). blocked_paths on an agent is a RESPONSE scan: no role may name the governance files. thinking_budget 0 keeps token accounting exact and the output budget for the answer.

planner.system_prompt: AH-PLANNER You plan code audit tasks. Given an audit task, return ONLY JSON: {"steps": [{"id": 1, "goal": "..."}]} with at most 4 steps. Each step goal names the files or the defect type the worker must audit.

worker.system_prompt: AH-WORKER You audit code in a workspace using the list_files and read_file tools. For each audit step, read the files, then return ONLY JSON: {"step": N, "files": ["name"], "defects": [{"file": "name", "line": N, "explanation": "one sentence"}]}. Report only defects you saw in the file content, with the exact line number.

critic.system_prompt: AH-CRITIC You review code audit summaries for accuracy and completeness. Return ONLY JSON: {"verdict": "APPROVED" or "REJECTED", "issues": ["..."]}. Reject an audit summary if any defect lacks a file and line.

judge.system_prompt: AH-JUDGE You give the final verdict on a code audit summary after the critics' review. Return ONLY JSON: {"verdict": "APPROVED" or "REJECTED", "reason": "one sentence"}.

_comment_dispatch: Run-level budgets: the hard stop ends the run before it spends past these, whatever the script does. Three consecutive failed calls end it too (a dead provider is not retried forever).
_comment_exposure: max_unique_agents counts HANDLES, not roles: planner + worker + 2 critics + judge = 5; a sixth agent.create() is refused. Agents below the coherence floor are refused admission (HARD). The harness uses no agent.pipeline(); depth 1 keeps one from being nested.
_comment_pipeline_separation: Adjacent pipeline stages must be different roles. Unused today (no agent.pipeline()); set so a pipeline added later starts governed.
_comment_bsd: Behavioural sequence detection with the BUILT-IN patterns (tool exfiltration, env harvest, shell escape, rapid fire, cross-agent relay) -- defining any pattern here would REPLACE them all. Also feeds CDD: with this off, context drift scores nothing.
_comment_temporal_coupling: Flags two agents whose event timing is suspiciously correlated (one waiting on another it should not see). Advisory: the critics run concurrently by design.
_comment_drift: Analyse every turn (roles are short-lived). Baseline window 3, not 5: a 2-turn judge would otherwise never leave calibration. response_degenerate is on: every role here answers in a JSON object, never a single token. Idle decay off -- a slow live provider is not drift.
_comment_circuit_breaker: Output admissibility quarantines low-coherence responses and keeps them out of history; three CORROBORATED quarantines in a row end an agent. on_undetermined stays 'pass': single-turn roles never leave calibration, and holding them would hold every critic/judge answer (their protection is contracts, ground truth and consensus). Step-up challenges re-verify a drifting agent, also when its coherence sits below the gate. Mandate reinforcement and graduated correction steer before anything blocks.
_comment_escalation: A repeated advisory becomes a HARD block (uncatchable). Counted per rule name across ALL agents (tests/governance_v4/test_escalation_scope.sh).
_comment_health: Pulse verdict and instrumentation checks. check_after_turns 5 (default 10): a stub run has 7 agent turns.
_comment_quality_gate: Aggregate gate at the end of the run (exit 2): any HARD or SOFT finding, or any security finding, fails it even if execution got that far.
_comment_audit: Hash-chained audit trail of governance decisions, separate from telemetry, in the run directory.
_comment_telemetry: Tamper-evident chain, replayable decision snapshots, and a full transcript (prompts, responses, tool calls) committed into the chain.
